mission: Engineering crawlspace. Per W1 Inversion 1, Kael approaches Desh — unprompted, not the Force-users, Desh specifically — with a practical observation he has made. Something Desh had missed: a pattern in the ship's power-cycle draw consistent with the bad conduit's failure mode, or an operational read on a Corridor-era architecture detail Desh catalogued earlier, or a communications artefact in the nav handshake. Short exchange. Desh absorbs it. Moves on. The hydrospanner passing follows from the shared work, not from being asked. Ben, passing the corridor, registers the exchange without interpreting it — an alliance he did not arrange.
why_now: The philosophical scene needed an exit. The ship needs its conduit fixed and the coalition needs a beat that is not an argument. The quietest scene in the chapter does the most lasting work. Kael, who at the galley spoke only when everyone else had committed, now — in a register where the Force is not the question — speaks first.
conflict: Kael has spent his life being used by institutions. Bringing Desh a practical observation is the first time he has initiated an operational act with someone who does not want anything from him spiritually. The internal question is not 'will Desh listen' — it is 'do I still know how to offer without being extracted.'
turning_point: Desh absorbs Kael's observation, folds it into the diagnosis, and asks Kael for the hydrospanner. Kael passes it after a beat of deliberate stillness. Smallest gesture, biggest meaning — the offer was Kael's, the ask is Desh's, neither one about the Force.
opening_hook: Kael finds Desh in the engineering crawlspace before Desh finds Kael. He has an observation — a pattern in the ship's power-cycle draw that has been nagging at him since the last transit — and he has decided to bring it to the man who will know what to do with it
closing_hook: Kael, watching Desh work, asks the oblique Force question; Desh deadpans it back into mechanical and interpersonal ship-reality. Kael almost smiles. Almost
emotional_trajectory: Residual tension -> Kael's self-directed approach -> quiet observation absorbed -> the smallest warmth

stakes.personal: Kael's first act of offering something to someone in the group on his own initiative
stakes.interpersonal: Kael/Desh quiet-alliance dyad established — the outsider and the practical man
stakes.external: Low — this is character breathing room; the pattern Kael named is a minor operational fact, not a reveal

setting: Aboard the Steady Returns — engineering crawlspace, Desh's domain
sensory_details: The ship's mechanical complaints; Desh's competent hands on familiar systems; Kael folded into an uncomfortable space designed for one person; the hydrospanner warm from Kael's grip before he passes it; Ben's shadow crossing the doorway of the corridor outside — passing, not stopping
action_beats: Kael approaches Desh with a specific practical observation about the ship's power-cycle draw — a pattern Desh had not yet isolated
Desh absorbs the observation, folds it into the diagnosis, and crawls into the engineering space to act on it
Kael folds himself into the crawlspace beside Desh and begins handing tools, the work absorbing him into it rather than the reverse
Kael passes the hydrospanner after a beat of deliberate stillness — the first thing anyone has asked him for that wasn't about the Force
Ben crosses the corridor outside on his way to the cockpit, sees the two of them working in the crawlspace, and moves on without stopping
promises_planted: Kael/Desh quiet alliance will pay implicitly at Ch 19 (articulated critique) and Ch 23 (commitment)
notes: Per W1 Inversion 1: Kael approaches Desh first, unprompted, with a practical observation. Kael's agency inverts here — he is no longer merely reacting to being treated well; he is initiating. The beat lives briefly (a sentence of observation, Desh's absorption, the work beginning) and reads as character texture, not plot signal. Per W1 anti-pattern guardrails: the beat does not carry an explicit reason; Ben's close-third does not underline with 'Kael had been acting differently lately' narration; the beat is not a scene of Kael's inner life but a short exchange Ben sees from the corridor. Thematically coherent with D4's character-differentiated unweaving architecture: Kael finds the Weave navigable; Desh doesn't feel it at all; neither is trapped in the standard-Jedi sensorium. This is the quiet-alliance opening. Ch 8 already carried a D7 Torin counter-current in a different register in s2 (silent intercept of Sera's pressure on Kael); the Kael/Desh beat is brief/practical and the two threads coexist per W1 distribution notes. Ben is mostly not on stage — the POV stays close to Kael through Ben's absence, with a single sight-through-the-doorway beat that holds Ben's close-third without violating single-POV discipline. Voice: Allston-channel warmth through Desh's operational flat matched against Kael's monk's brevity. Let the hydrospanner do what words would spoil. Anti-pattern: no interiority paragraph explaining Kael's first experience of initiating — the gesture is the exposition. Per R11, no late-Ben analytical register imported here. Primary anchor: Allston (two-voice distinction); supporting anchor: Zahn (workmanlike procedural frame). Stover not permitted this scene.
